risks.title: validator consensus key theft, cloning, rollback, or double-sign
risks.scenario: a stolen or restored signer signs conflicting votes or loses last-sign state
prevention: no key in images, snapshots, or support bundles
risks.residualRisk: validator compromise remains possible; public release is blocked until custody and recovery are exercised

risks.title: malicious validator censorship, quorum halt, partition, or conflicting commit
risks.scenario: one-third-or-more power withholds votes or partitions peers; Byzantine power violates the trust envelope
risks.residualRisk: CometBFT cannot guarantee safety after its Byzantine-power assumption fails

risks.title: nondeterministic app, EVM, precompile, or module execution splits consensus
risks.scenario: different validators compute different app hashes from the same committed input
recovery: root-cause and versioned upgrade or new genesis
risks.residualRisk: upstream or Torium composition bugs can still cause consensus failure

risks.title: genesis supply, allocation, denom, power, or identifier tampering
risks.scenario: a modified genesis mints, reallocates, truncates voting power, or changes replay domains
detection: bank, EVM native, and Solidity facade conservation tests
recovery: allocate new public IDs after abandoned genesis
risks.residualRisk: a trusted distribution channel can still present the wrong genesis unless clients pin checksums

risks.title: unauthorized governance, parameter mutation, privileged action, or binary upgrade
risks.scenario: an undocumented key or proposal changes consensus, supply, fees, modules, contracts, or executable code
risks.residualRisk: legitimate governance can still approve harmful changes; social review remains required

risks.title: source, dependency, builder, artifact, image, or provenance compromise
risks.scenario: a malicious dependency or builder produces a binary different from reviewed source
risks.residualRisk: upstream signed releases and registries remain external trust dependencies

risks.title: secret, mnemonic, validator key, API token, or credential leaks into artifacts
risks.scenario: source, logs, images, fixtures, examples, containers, or support bundles expose credentials
risks.residualRisk: pattern scanning cannot prove absence of every encoded or novel credential

risks.title: poisoned, stale, corrupted, or untrusted snapshot, backup, or state-sync input
risks.scenario: a node restores incorrect state or trusts an attacker-selected height and hash
risks.residualRisk: local artifacts are self-checked but public clients still need an authentic initial trust anchor and operator policy from #116

risks.title: replay across reset, environment, chain ID, account sequence, or signing domain
risks.scenario: an old signed transaction becomes valid after reset or a client signs for the wrong network
risks.residualRisk: deterministic valueless local resets deliberately reuse IDs and require explicit cleanup

risks.title: RPC, WebSocket, REST, gRPC, debug, batch, log, or trace denial of service
risks.scenario: expensive calls, broad logs, batches, subscriptions, traces, or bodies exhaust node resources
prevention: caps, timeouts, quotas, origins, and reverse proxy
risks.residualRisk: permissionless reads and transaction submission always expose a resource-cost surface

risks.title: P2P eclipse, peer poisoning, asymmetric partition, or validator address exposure
risks.scenario: an attacker monopolizes peers, isolates validators, or targets exposed consensus nodes
risks.residualRisk: a sufficiently powerful network adversary can delay or partition communication

risks.title: faucet abuse, budget exhaustion, queue flood, nonce contention, or signer compromise
risks.scenario: bots bypass simple rate limits or compromise a signer with excessive authority
prevention: idempotency, layered limits, bounded queue, global budget
risks.residualRisk: public valueless tokens remain attractive to automated abuse and address farms

risks.title: nonce gaps, fee replacement, mempool eviction, propagation, or lifecycle misreporting
risks.scenario: RPC acceptance is mistaken for retention or network-wide replacement and clients lose transaction state
prevention: bounded local app pool and explicit timeouts
same-nonce replacement requires at least 10 percent more fee cap and tip cap at the receiving node
detection: dropped, replaced, unknown, and halt diagnostics
risks.residualRisk: distributed mempools cannot provide a single authoritative pending view

risks.title: explorer or indexer serves incomplete, stale, spoofed, or noncanonical data
risks.scenario: users or SDKs trust an indexer view that missed logs, traces, resets, or canonical blocks
risks.residualRisk: trace support is partial and indexed derived data can lag canonical state

risks.title: system contract or precompile authorization, reentrancy, accounting, or spoofed-event failure
risks.scenario: crafted call sequences bypass access control, double-claim, corrupt accounting, or emit trusted-looking false events
detection: fuzz, invariant, differential, and malicious-token tests
risks.residualRisk: permissionless composability creates call sequences not covered by examples

risks.title: deployment registry, ABI, address, bytecode, or environment metadata tampering
risks.scenario: SDK or docs direct users to wrong code, address, ABI, chain, or deployment transaction
risks.residualRisk: clients that pin stale metadata remain vulnerable until upgraded

risks.title: fee, gas, payload, state-growth, or transaction-spam economic denial of service
risks.scenario: cheap or pathological transactions saturate blocks, storage, execution, queries, or evidence capacity
prevention: 1 gwei EIP-1559 floor and 1 atorium per gas local EVM priority floor
30 million block gas with 15 million target and 25 million transaction and call cap
5 MiB block and RPC body, 128 KiB EVM transaction, 256 KiB Cosmos transaction, and 100-request batch caps
bounded application mempool slots, queues, lifetime, and Cosmos transaction count
detection: four-validator local fee, payload, saturation, base-fee, and accounting acceptance suite
risks.residualRisk: sustained state growth remains unbounded over time and local measurements do not establish public throughput or economic security

risks.title: 18-decimal supply, staking power, reward, fee, or rounding invariant failure
risks.scenario: PowerReduction truncation, dust, repeated partial operations, or conversion errors alter balances or voting power
prevention: bank-backed native Solidity facade without representation conversion
detection: power, pool, reward, and fee reconciliation
native facade balance and total-supply reconciliation
risks.residualRisk: bounded base-unit share dust remains explicit; public economic-security review remains a release gate

risks.title: node or validator backup and recovery causes rollback, stale state, or evidence loss
risks.scenario: an operator restores a signer or database behind its last signed height or loses slashable evidence
recovery: rebuild node state from trusted source
risks.residualRisk: human recovery error remains a material double-sign vector

risks.title: host, container, node profile, debug interface, or runtime isolation compromise
risks.scenario: an exposed service or over-privileged container reaches keys, state, host, or validator network
risks.residualRisk: kernel, cloud control-plane, and hardware compromise remain external dependencies

risks.title: known or novel upstream dependency vulnerability and abandoned maintenance line
risks.scenario: Cosmos EVM, CometBFT, Cosmos SDK, go-ethereum, compiler, or build dependency contains an exploitable flaw
risks.residualRisk: pre-1.0 Cosmos EVM and its go-ethereum fork can introduce rapid compatibility and security change

risks.title: spoofed endpoint, wrong chain, inconsistent RPC semantics, or unsafe client fallback
risks.scenario: a client trusts an attacker RPC, wrong chain ID, unsupported safe/finalized behavior, or invented public fallback
risks.residualRisk: users may manually trust malicious custom-network metadata outside Torium control

risks.title: logs, telemetry, screenshots, debug dumps, or support bundles leak secrets or sensitive topology
risks.scenario: diagnostic artifacts contain keys, tokens, environment values, validator addresses, or exploitable host details
risks.residualRisk: novel encodings, memory dumps, and human screenshots can evade pattern rules

risks.title: CI, branch, tag, reviewer, cache, or release credential bypass
risks.scenario: an attacker bypasses required checks/review or poisons cache and publishes trusted-looking output
risks.residualRisk: repository and CI provider administrator compromise remains an external trust risk

risks.title: reward proof, attestation, role, domain, or event spoofing causes unauthorized contract state
risks.scenario: a proof is replayed or forged, an attestor role is misused, or an event is treated as truth without state verification
prevention: issuer-scoped sender identity and replay keys
risks.residualRisk: reward publishers and permissionless issuers remain trusted for the statements and datasets they commit

invariants.statement: all honest validators produce the same app hash from identical committed input
faults inside the trust threshold never produce conflicting committed blocks
genesis regeneration preserves checksum, total supply, denom, chain IDs, allocations, integer validator power, and one bank-backed native facade
only ratified governance authority and a versioned rehearsed plan can perform privileged upgrades
reviewed source and immutable inputs reproduce byte-identical signed release artifacts with SBOM and provenance
tracked source and every generated diagnostic staging directory pass a redacted six-surface secret scan before publication
snapshot, backup, state-sync, and restart recovery preserve trusted genesis, height, hash, and app state without manual edits
transactions cannot cross public replay domains and local reset reuse is explicit and artifact-clean
public RPC profiles expose only approved namespaces and remain bounded under adversarial method, body, batch, log, trace, and subscription load
peer loss and asymmetric partitions match the trust manifest and validators are not directly exposed by public RPC topology
faucet replay, concurrency, address farming, queue pressure, RPC failure, and signer compromise cannot exceed configured budget or authority
transaction clients expose submitted, pending, committed, dropped, replaced, and unknown without promising retention, RBF, or bounded inclusion
explorer and indexer views reconcile canonical height, hash, logs, receipts, reset markers, and documented trace gaps
precompiles and system contracts preserve authorization, atomic revert, accounting, replay, and event-to-state invariants under arbitrary call sequences
deployment registry chain ID, address, ABI, transaction, bytecode, and runtime code hash match the local chain and packed SDK
fee, gas, payload, log, trace, and state-growth limits keep validators live at the ratified capacity envelope
18-decimal balances, shares, power, fees, rewards, commission, slashes, and dust reconcile across repeated boundary operations
key backup, restore, rotation, and compromise response never starts a stale cloned signer or loses accountability evidence
node, container, host, debug, observability, and support profiles enforce least privilege and emit no prohibited secret
every dependency and release candidate has a current SBOM, advisory result, upstream delta review, and tested upgrade or rejection decision

releaseGates.rule: no high or critical risk lacks prevention, detection, recovery, owners, tests, triggers, and explicit residual risk
tracked source, images, logs, fixtures, examples, containers, and extracted support-bundle staging pass prohibited-secret gates
multi-validator deterministic app-hash, EVM, module, precompile, genesis, supply, power, and conformance tests pass
all trust-model chaos scenarios pass and no tolerated fault produces a conflicting commit
system contracts complete fuzz, invariant, access-control, deployment-registry, and audit-readiness checks
snapshot, state-sync, backup, key compromise, restore, and upgrade interruption runbooks are exercised
reproducible signed artifacts, checksums, SBOMs, provenance, protected release workflow, and second security reviewer are in place
public-testnet faucet signer isolation, budgets, abuse controls, monitoring, and emergency procedures pass locally
external audit and launch security review have no unresolved high or critical finding
public deployment remains blocked until issue 127 receives explicit current approval after all prerequisites

reviewTriggers: protocol, chain ID, denom, PowerReduction, module, precompile, fee, mempool, or finality change
validator, key custody, governance, upgrade, snapshot, state-sync, RPC, P2P, faucet, explorer, contract, CI, release, or support-bundle design change
new public endpoint, independent operator, infrastructure provider, artifact, package, or deployment environment
security advisory, audit finding, secret finding, app-hash mismatch, conflicting header, supply mismatch, exploit, sustained outage, or recovery failure
any proposal to integrate the existing Torium product backend or add PoP, IBC, bridge, L2, live value, or mainnet behavior

riskAcceptance.localDevelopmentRule: documented residual risk may be exercised only with valueless loopback or isolated local infrastructure
riskAcceptance.publicRule: high and critical risks remain public-release blockers until owner tests and issue 126 review pass
